key_insight: EvoRouter learns to configure multi-agent systems by distilling reusable execution insights into a routing policy that balances accuracy and compute cost.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets more efficient query serving by jointly selecting models, collaboration modes, agent counts, interaction rounds, and skills.
method: An expert periodically extracts conditional routing insights from performance–cost feedback across task trajectories.
A privileged teacher uses insights and execution feedback to provide token-level supervision on the router’s own planning trajectories.
Cost-aware reinforcement learning updates the router, whose new executions feed the next insight-extraction cycle.
evidence_signal: Across 19 in-domain datasets spanning five domains, EvoRouter reports 68.69% average accuracy, beating the strongest routing baseline by 7.23 percentage points while reducing inference compute cost by 50.95%; evaluation also includes two out-of-domain benchmarks.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify the training overhead of expert insight extraction and teacher supervision, which may affect overall cost savings.
paper_title: EvoRouter: Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Routing via Insight-Guided On-Policy Distillation
